newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on China corn selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on China corn selling.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower, buffeted by gyrations in the soybean pit and ultimately pressured by confirmation China was selling corn, traders said.
"It was following beans and had some bearish news with China selling corn to South Korea," a trader said.
Traders in Seoul Tuesday said South Korea bought 126,500 tonnes of Chinese corn and was seeking another 190,000 tonnes.
The corn market took in stride USDA's March supply/demand data because traders and analysts had anticipated no change in the government's carryout tally for 1996-97 U.S. corn.
USDA early Tuesday left unchanged at 959 million bushels its outlook for the corn carryover during the current (1996-97) marketing year slated to end on August 31.

USDA dropped to 8.5 million tonnes from the previous 9.5 million its estimate for South African corn production during 1996-97. It left unchanged the outlook for Argentina's crop at 14.5 million tonnes and Argentine exports were left intact at 8.75 million tonnes.
Corn closed 1-1/2 to four cents per bushel lower, with March down 3-1/2 at $3.08-1/2.
The corn market also was pressured by talk of possible feed grade wheat to be shipped into the U.S. from Canada.
Technicians early Tuesday cited first resistance in the March at $3.16 a bushel and second resistance at $3.26. The session high for March was $3.09-3/4.
First support was at $3.05-3/4 and second support was at $2.95-1/2. The session low was $3.06-1/2.

Chartists said the four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals for the corn market. The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the March closed at 74 percent. The trade views a market as overbought with an RSI of 70 or more and oversold at 30 or less.

Refco Inc sold nine million bushels of May and sold three million bushels of July, traders said. Griffin Trading sold 4.5 million bushels of July and Farmers Commodities Corp bought two million bushels of May, the traders said.
Cargill Inc spread 2.5 million May/March and Produce Grain did two million March/May, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts, below the 102,424 traded Monday.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, above the 14,146 traded Monday.

In corn options Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 500 May $3.00 calls and sold 1,000 May $3.20 calls at 2-1/2 cents, sources aid. Cargill Investor Services sold 500 July $3.30 calls at 9-9-1/2 cents and E.D. and F. Man International bought 350 December $2.90 puts at 23-1/2 cents.
